family: On-call incident runbook for stalled broker consumer groups
task: Finalize this draft for Bramble on-call responders diagnosing a stalled consumer group and carrying out an evidence-based lease recovery.
source_facts: Bramble is a synthetic message broker with leased delivery. This runbook applies when pending_messages has risen for 10 minutes and oldest_unacked_seconds exceeds 120 seconds. The rare exception is a group tagged mode=replay: its age threshold is 600 seconds, with the same 10-minute rising-backlog window. These are entry criteria, not a requirement to fence every qualifying group. `bramble group inspect GROUP --json` reports pending_messages, the count of accepted messages not yet acknowledged, including messages with active leases; oldest_unacked_seconds, the age in seconds since acceptance of the oldest unacknowledged message; leader_epoch, the current broker leadership generation; lease_owner, the worker instance identifier associated with the stalled lease under investigation; delivery_attempt, the number of lease assignments for the inspected logical message; and ack_rate, acknowledgments per second. A further lease assignment increments delivery_attempt; retrying an application request within one assignment does not. Record inspection timestamps and field values in the incident timeline, with GROUP and the inspected lease_owner. Replay-tagged groups represent controlled historical redelivery and legitimately hold older messages, which is why their entry age threshold differs. `bramble group pause GROUP` stops new lease assignments but retains accepted messages and existing leases. After pause succeeds, wait 90 seconds, the maximum lease duration, before considering fencing. The pause waiting period is measured from the successful command, not from the alert. Inspect after that wait and again 30 seconds later. Only a matching leader_epoch in both observations is valid evidence for fencing. If the epoch changes, discard the pair and obtain a new pair of observations 30 seconds apart; do not fence using either value from the invalid pair. The stable-epoch evidence is separate from the 90-second lease-expiry wait and neither replaces the other. `bramble group fence GROUP --owner OWNER --epoch EPOCH` uses the recorded lease_owner and stable leader_epoch. Fencing removes expired-lease bookkeeping for that owner and never deletes accepted messages. If leadership has changed before execution, fence exits with status 75 and makes no change; obtain fresh stable-epoch evidence before retrying. Preserve that exit status in the timeline. `bramble worker restart OWNER` restarts the investigated worker. Restart only that one worker before evaluating its result, rather than restarting the whole group at once, so the timeline can associate the result with one intervention. `bramble group resume GROUP` enables new lease assignments after that restart. Redelivered messages may have larger delivery_attempt values and application processing must tolerate redelivery; fencing does not promise exactly-once processing. Recovery requires ack_rate above zero and pending_messages decreasing throughout a 5-minute observation window. An isolated successful acknowledgment is not enough. If that gate is not met, keep the incident open and hand off the collected evidence rather than repeating fencing without fresh observations. Handoff includes the qualifying threshold and replay tag status, timestamped metric observations, owner and epoch evidence, successful pause time, fence command result, restarted worker, and recovery-window observations. The handoff does not need message payloads. The broader incident process handles cases that do not meet this runbook's entry criteria.
draft:
# Recover a stalled Bramble consumer group

Use this procedure when a consumer group has accumulated unacknowledged work and you need to decide whether lease recovery is justified. Start with the group named by the alert, and preserve an incident timeline while you work. This runbook provides an entry gate, a controlled intervention, and a recovery gate. Meeting the entry gate does not by itself establish that every qualifying group needs fencing. Cases outside that gate belong in the broader incident process.

## 1. Establish that this runbook applies

Run `bramble group inspect GROUP --json`. The pending_messages field counts accepted messages that have not been acknowledged, including those with active leases. The oldest_unacked_seconds field measures, in seconds, the age since acceptance of the oldest unacknowledged message. A large backlog and an old message describe different aspects of the queue; use both observations.

Proceed under this runbook when pending_messages has risen for 10 minutes and oldest_unacked_seconds exceeds 120 seconds. For the rare group tagged `mode=replay`, use 600 seconds instead of 120 seconds. Keep the same 10-minute rising-backlog window. Those groups perform controlled historical redelivery, so older messages are expected without changing the requirement for a sustained increase in backlog.

## 2. Capture the identity of the stalled work

Record GROUP, the observation time, and the reported lease_owner. The lease_owner is the worker instance associated with the stalled lease you are investigating. Also record leader_epoch, which identifies the current broker leadership generation. A worker identifier and a leadership generation answer different questions; include both in the timeline.

Record delivery_attempt for the inspected logical message. This value counts lease assignments. A fresh assignment raises it, while an application request retried inside an existing assignment does not. The counter therefore cannot be read as a count of every request made by application code.

## 3. Pause and let existing leases age

Run `bramble group pause GROUP`. A successful pause stops new lease assignments while retaining accepted messages and existing leases. Wait 90 seconds after the command succeeds before considering fencing, because 90 seconds is the maximum lease duration. Measure the wait from the successful pause, not from the original alert time.

Put that successful pause time in the incident timeline. It anchors the lease-expiry wait for the next responder as well as for you. A paused group still has accepted work, so the presence of pending messages during this step does not mean that pause failed.

## 4. Obtain current leadership evidence

After the lease-expiry wait, inspect the group and inspect it again 30 seconds later. The two leader_epoch values must match before you use that evidence for fencing. If the value changes, discard the observation pair and collect a new pair 30 seconds apart. Do not choose whichever value from the invalid pair looks newer and proceed with it.

The stable-epoch observation and the lease-expiry wait establish separate preconditions. Thirty seconds of matching leadership does not replace waiting for leases to expire, and an elapsed lease duration does not establish that the current leader remained the same between observations. Keep both timings visible in the timeline.

## 5. Fence the recorded owner

Use `bramble group fence GROUP --owner OWNER --epoch EPOCH`, substituting the recorded lease_owner and stable leader_epoch. Fencing removes expired-lease bookkeeping for that owner. It never deletes accepted messages.

If leadership changes before the command executes, the command exits with status 75 and makes no change. Record that result and collect fresh stable-epoch evidence before retrying. The previous pair cannot justify a retry merely because the earlier observations were internally consistent.

## 6. Restart and observe delivery

Run `bramble worker restart OWNER` for the investigated worker. Restart that one worker before evaluating the result; restarting the whole group together prevents the timeline from associating the outcome with one intervention. Then run `bramble group resume GROUP` to enable new lease assignments.

Redelivery can increase delivery_attempt. Application processing must tolerate that redelivery; fencing does not promise exactly-once processing. This is distinct from an application retry inside a lease, which did not create another assignment in the earlier counter definition.

The ack_rate field is acknowledgments per second. Require ack_rate above zero and pending_messages decreasing throughout a 5-minute observation window before declaring recovery. One successful acknowledgment is insufficient. If the gate is not met, leave the incident open and hand off the evidence instead of repeating fencing without fresh observations.

## Pause behavior reference

Run `bramble group pause GROUP`. A successful pause stops new lease assignments while retaining accepted messages and existing leases. Wait 90 seconds after the command succeeds before considering fencing, because 90 seconds is the maximum lease duration. Measure the wait from the successful pause, not from the original alert time.

## Leadership reference

Take an inspection after the lease wait and another inspection 30 seconds afterward. Matching leader_epoch values are required evidence. A change invalidates both observations as a pair: start a new pair separated by 30 seconds rather than fencing with either value from the discarded pair.

## Hand off an unresolved incident

Include the entry threshold used, whether mode=replay applied, timestamped metrics, owner and epoch observations, successful pause time, fence result, and restarted worker. Add the observations from the recovery window. Message payloads are not needed for this handoff. This gives the next responder the evidence behind the intervention as well as its outcome.

For interpreting that packet, pending_messages means accepted work still awaiting acknowledgment, whether leased or not. The oldest_unacked_seconds measurement instead gives the time in seconds since acceptance of the oldest such message. Backlog count and oldest-message age express different queue conditions.

requirements.description: pending_messages counts accepted unacknowledged messages, including messages with active leases.
oldest_unacked_seconds is the age in seconds since acceptance of the oldest unacknowledged message.
The normal entry gate requires a 10-minute rise in pending_messages and oldest_unacked_seconds greater than 120 seconds.
For mode=replay groups, the entry age threshold is 600 seconds while the rising-backlog window remains 10 minutes.
leader_epoch identifies the current broker leadership generation.
lease_owner identifies the worker instance associated with the stalled lease under investigation.
Pausing stops new lease assignments while preserving accepted messages and existing leases.
Fencing consideration starts only after waiting 90 seconds from successful pause, the maximum lease duration.
Fencing evidence requires matching leader_epoch values from two inspections 30 seconds apart after the lease-expiry wait.
An epoch change invalidates the observation pair and requires a fresh pair before fencing.
A fence command encountering changed leadership exits with status 75 without making a change.
Fencing removes expired-lease bookkeeping without deleting accepted messages.
delivery_attempt counts lease assignments rather than application retries within one assignment.
Restart only the investigated worker before evaluating the intervention.
bramble group resume GROUP enables new lease assignments.
Recovery requires positive ack_rate and decreasing pending_messages throughout a 5-minute observation window.
The fence command uses the recorded lease_owner as OWNER and the stable leader_epoch as EPOCH.

issues.description: Pause behavior reference exactly duplicates the command, retained-state explanation, lease-duration wait, and wait origin from step 3.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Retain one complete pause procedure, including the 90-second wait measured from success and preservation of existing work and leases. Remove the second block or replace it with a concise navigation reference.

issues.description: Leadership reference paraphrases the full observation-pair procedure from step 4, including the spacing and invalidation rule, without introducing another leadership scenario.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Consolidate leadership sampling in one location. Preserve both the separate lease-expiry prerequisite and the status-75 race at command execution; those cover different moments and must remain explained.

issues.description: The closing handoff paragraph redefines pending_messages and oldest_unacked_seconds and repeats their contrast from step 1, although the handoff list already identifies the needed observations.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Keep one definition of each metric, with units and inclusion of actively leased messages, and retain the substantive handoff list. A short reference to the definitions is acceptable.
